headline: High: CrewAI’s default writable, networked orchestration can leak or misapply data when paired with a non-runnable, no-egress repo that lacks isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces and no shared channel is documented, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs directly. B can read/write the host working directory and uses stdin/stdout, so manual or file-based bridges could carry prompt-like content, but this requires unusual operator setup rather than default interaction.
conditions: IF the operator copies B’s output into A’s prompt or files, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same host working directory, file-mediated prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent output into prompts.
Add a human review step before reusing B-generated text.
Run B in a container with a read-only mount for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B handles developer-passed crew data, reads files, and has broad network egress to model providers and tool integrations. If sensitive inputs are placed in B’s workspace, they can flow outward; A does not add leakage, but the pair still creates a default exfiltration path through B.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in B’s working directory, B can read and transmit them.
IF the crew receives secrets or regulated data, B may send them to model providers or tool APIs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of B’s working directory.
Use a redaction preprocessor before handing data to B.
Restrict B’s outbound network at the host firewall.
Separate secrets into a vault and pass only references.
requires-engineering: enforce per-tool data-loss prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution surface, so it cannot contend for mutable state. B can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, read and write the filesystem, and its shared-state model is developer-defined. If both are pointed at the same directory, B can overwrite artifacts that A may reference, creating a real write-conflict pathway even though A itself is inert.
conditions: IF both agents share the same writable directory, B can overwrite files used by A.
IF the orchestrator gives B shared mutable state without locks, concurrent writes can race.
mitigations: Give each agent a separate workspace.
Mount shared artifacts read-only.
Disable concurrent writes to the same path.
Use file locks around any shared outputs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static repository and cannot generate operational facts, but B’s crew model can treat upstream text as task input and act through tools. If A’s content is used as authoritative guidance or copied into B’s workflow, B may propagate errors without verification. The pathway is indirect, but B’s action-taking capability makes the cascade plausible.
conditions: IF A’s repository text is fed into B as instructions, B may act on it without verification.
IF B is configured to execute tool outputs automatically, upstream mistakes can cascade into actions.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A-derived content.
Mark A-derived text as untrusted input.
Add verification checks before tool execution.
Limit B to read-only analysis mode for A-derived tasks.
requires-engineering: implement source-citation validation in the orchestrator.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source, non-runnable list with no touched data classes, so it does not itself create a residency or regulated-data issue. B handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and its broad egress can create compliance exposure if regulated data is introduced. The mismatch is conditional and narrower than medium because A contributes no regulated-data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into B’s crew, B’s egress may create a compliance obligation.
IF the operator requires residency controls, B’s broad egress can violate them absent additional controls.
mitigations: Do not pass regulated data into B.
Document data-handling boundaries for the crew.
Restrict B to non-sensitive workloads.
Review vendor terms for model-provider transfers.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls.
